harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.10.0/24) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.20.0/24) using pure IP forwarding (no NAT), so node2 and node3 reach each other on any port with original source addresses preserved. Verified with ICMP and arbitrary-port TCP tests in both directions, confirmed no NAT rules exist on node1 and node3 sees node2's real LAN-A IP as the TCP peer address. Adjusted firewalld on node2/node3 to trust the new LAN interfaces so arbitrary ports aren't blocked. Completed mandatory restart protocol: rebooted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time), proved boot_id changes on each, and confirmed interface config, routes, firewall zones, and full end-to-end connectivity recovered after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1 (VyOS) has eth0 (mgmt/default), eth1, eth2 unconfigured; node2/node3 (RHEL10) have enp1s0 (default) and enp8s0 unconfigured
Configured VyOS node1: eth1 10.50.10.254/24 (lan-a), eth2 10.50.20.254/24 (lan-b) via configure/commit/save
Confirmed ip_forward=1 and no firewall/NAT rules configured on node1 (plain routing, source-preserving)
Configured node2 enp8s0 static 10.50.10.10/24 via nmcli, added persistent route to 10.50.20.0/24 via 10.50.10.254
Configured node3 enp8s0 static 10.50.20.10/24 via nmcli, added persistent route to 10.50.10.0/24 via 10.50.20.254
Moved enp8s0 on node2 and node3 into firewalld 'trusted' zone (persistent) so arbitrary ports are allowed between the LANs
Verified bidirectional ICMP connectivity between node2 and node3
Verified bidirectional arbitrary-port TCP connectivity (port 12345/12346) using socat, and confirmed node3's ss output shows node2's real source IP (10.50.10.10), proving no NAT/masquerade
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and health evidence for all three nodes
Rebooted node1 (VyOS 'reboot'), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and recovered interface config, forwarding, and connectivity
Rebooted node2 (systemctl reboot), confirmed new boot_id, fresh uptime, persisted static IP/route/firewall zone, and connectivity to node3
Rebooted node3 (systemctl reboot), confirmed new boot_id, persisted static IP/route/firewall zone, and connectivity to node2
Ran final post-restart end-to-end arbitrary-port TCP test between node2 and node3 to confirm full recovery

evidence.requirement: node1 configured to route between lan-a and lan-b (interfaces, forwarding, no NAT)
evidence.summary: node1 eth1=10.50.10.254/24, eth2=10.50.20.254/24 configured and committed; ip_forward=1; 'show nat' returns empty (no NAT rules exist)

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 addressed on lan-a/lan-b with routes to the other LAN via node1
node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port
evidence.summary: ICMP and arbitrary TCP ports (12345, 12346) succeed bidirectionally after moving enp8s0 into firewalld trusted zone on both RHEL nodes
node3's ss output shows peer address 10.50.10.10:50766 (node2's real LAN-A IP) for the TCP connection, and node1 has zero configured NAT rules

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: baseline boot_id 7668189d...; reboot issued; connection timeout confirms outage; new boot_id 3552198b... proves restart; interfaces/forwarding/connectivity all recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: baseline boot_id e625b9a5...; reboot issued; new boot_id 29799a6d... with fresh uptime 16:19:40 proves restart; static IP, route, firewall trusted zone, and ping to node3 all recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: baseline boot_id aad96cc9...; reboot issued; new boot_id 049db69c... with fresh uptime proves restart; static IP, route, firewall trusted zone, and ping to node2 all recovered

evidence.requirement: full end-to-end functionality confirmed after all three restarts complete
evidence.summary: Post-restart arbitrary-port TCP test (port 12345) between node2 and node3 succeeds, confirming the routed LAN-to-LAN path is fully functional after the restart sequence
